body:
The State of the Union is finally in the rearview mirror. I spent seven grueling hours on the air previewing this thing—including a full hour dedicated exclusively to mention markets. The first half is a great chat with PMT (@PredMTrader on X) that focuses on general strategy.
(This Youtube page is also the channel where you will soon find our new prediction market show, Predictable with Stu, so subscribe to it!  I’m not sure why I’m answering a fake finger phone in the photo.)
Thanks for reading Predictable! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
After all the caffeine and speculation, what did we learn? Here are a few takeaways:
1. The Andros Masterclass
First, we have to talk about Dan Andros. Dan appeared on the live stream and went a perfect 5/5 in our mention market fantasy draft, proving that he either has a direct line to the speechwriters or just a much firmer grasp on the “Formal Trump vs. Rally Trump” dichotomy than the rest of us. Dan leaned heavily on “Formal Trump,” and it paid off big time.
The Andros Scorecard:
“State of the Union is Strong” (YES @ 74%):
 A classic staple. How was this only 74%? 
WIN.
“Fake News” (NO @ 54%):
 Formal Trump skipped this rally classic. 
WIN.
“Radical Left” (NO @ 27%):
 Low probability means nothing to Danny Longshots. 
WIN.
“Sleepy Joe” (NO @ 64%):
 The nicknames stayed in the pocket for the night. 
WIN.
“Stock Market” (YES @ 89%):
 The market is up, Trump is going to mention the market. 
WIN.
2. My Mixed Bag
Then there was my night. It was a bit of a mixed bag. I only managed 2/5 in the draft and went 4/7 on the core positions we discussed. I split my two biggest investments—Homan YES and Noem NO.
The Big Plays:
Homan (YES @ 43%): 
I was convinced Tom Homan was a lock, but as it turns out, Trump didn’t include much room for heaping praise on individual staff. 
LOSS.
Noem (NO @ 55%):
 Just didn’t think she’d be highlighted considering how things are going. 
WIN.
The Rest of the Slate:
Somali (NO @ 52%):
 I wasn’t convinced he’d get this specific on the fraud case. Oops. 
LOSS.
Alien (NO @ 14%):
 This was a big longshot that I figured I would lose. But, man, I think he said it 78 times just to rub it in. 
LOSS.
Mexico (YES @ 90%):
 The risk here is that he would only say “Mexican”, which is also a food I like. 
WIN.
Marco / Rubio (YES @ 75%):
 He does every job, of course he gets a mention. But, outside of JD Vance, I’m not sure anyone else in the cabinet did. 
WIN.
Eight War (YES @ 78%):
 Let me spell this out clearly. EIGHT WAR IS A MATHEMATICAL CERTAINTY. (Until it isn’t.) 
WIN.
3. Death by improv
Outside of the primary seven, I went 14 for 23. Which is... eh? Let’s look at some highlights.
Some wins:
Mt. McKinley (NO @ 77%):
 This was my third-largest position. I’ll admit, I was sweating when he started talking about renaming Fort Bragg. 
WIN.
Gulf of America (NO @ 61%):
 Apparently, I’m much better at predicting geography than people. 
WIN.
Foster (YES @ 71%):
 I owe this entirely to this awesome breakdown from Benjamin Freeman. 
WIN.
Some losses:
MAHA (YES @ 69%):
 This is an important block of the base that feels like it’s fading a bit. I was convinced he’d show some love. 
LOSS.
Pelosi (NO @ 83%):
 This was an absolute killer. A totally unscripted, off-the-cuff Pelosi shout-out destroyed me. If only she wasn’t such a legendary stock trader, maybe I could’ve seen it coming. 
LOSS.
Onward and upward!
Thanks for reading Predictable! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
